# Linux: compile or install Mixxx with Beat This!

Run as your normal user. The script never calls `sudo` or a system package
manager. Mixxx, the Python virtual environment, the official checkpoint and
the optional starter are stored in user-owned directories.

From a checkout or extracted source archive:

```sh
python3 tools/install-linux.py
```

The script asks whether to **only compile** (`b`) or **install with a
starter** (`i`). Both modes install the isolated Python runtime and Beat
This! dependencies, download and verify `final0`, and configure its absolute
paths in a separate Mixxx profile. A new profile selects Beat This! and
**Auto** grid mode. Existing Auto/Constant/Variable choices are preserved.

- **Build:** compiles Mixxx and prints the complete terminal command,
  including resource and profile paths. Copy that command into your own
  shortcut if desired. It does not run `cmake --install` or create starters.
- **Install:** also runs `cmake --install` into the local prefix, creates
  the command `~/.local/bin/mixxx-beat-this`, and adds **Mixxx (Beat This!)**
  to the desktop application menu. The starter uses absolute paths; it
  requires neither virtual-environment activation nor a shell PATH change.

For a non-interactive invocation, explicitly select the mode:

```sh
python3 tools/install-linux.py --mode build
python3 tools/install-linux.py --mode install
```

## Standalone download

The same script can be downloaded on its own. It clones this development
branch when no adjacent Mixxx/Beat This! sources are found:

```sh
curl -fLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabba43/mixxx/feat/beat-this-variable-tempo/tools/install-linux.py
python3 install-linux.py
```

Review the downloaded script before executing it. The default repository
is `https://github.com/gabba43/mixxx.git`, branch
`feat/beat-this-variable-tempo`. Use `--repository` and `--ref` to select a
different repository and branch/tag for a **new** clone. The selected ref
must contain the Beat This! integration.

Existing sources are used unchanged, including local edits. The script
does not reset, pull, switch branches or overwrite an unrelated directory.
It recognizes source archives too; Git is needed only when cloning.
`--source-dir /path/to/mixxx` selects existing sources explicitly or clones
into that path if it does not exist.

## Native prerequisites and supported systems

```sh
python3 tools/install-linux.py --print-deps
```

The installer runs on glibc Linux, with pinned CPU PyTorch packages for
x86_64 and aarch64. The complete installation has been exercised on Debian
13 x86_64; other distributions and aarch64 have not been tested here.
Native Alpine/musl, 32-bit Linux and other CPU architectures are unsupported
by this pinned runtime. No CUDA installation is needed.

Python 3.8 or newer can run the installer itself. It finds an installed
CPython **3.10, 3.11 or 3.12** for the isolated Beat This! environment, or
accepts `--python /path/to/python3.12`. These versions have wheels for the
pinned PyTorch 2.5.1 runtime. The script does not install a Python interpreter;
its `venv` and `ensurepip` modules must be available (Debian/Ubuntu:
the matching `python3.X-venv` package). Python libraries and Beat This! are
installed automatically into a venv, never into system Python.

The native build requires CMake >= 3.22, a C++20 compiler, pkg-config,
Make or Ninja, and Mixxx's development libraries. CMake checks the libraries
before compilation and Python/model installation. Allow several GB of free
disk space; a first native build can take considerably longer than Python
setup. Default parallelism is at most four compiler processes; reduce it
with `--jobs 2` on machines with limited memory.

Native dependencies are distribution packages, or an existing user-local
toolchain supplied through `--cmake-arg`. They are **not** automatically
installed system-wide. If they are missing, an administrator must provide
them, or you must supply a user-local development environment first.

- **Debian/Ubuntu:** the current native package list is in
  [packaging/debian/control.in](packaging/debian/control.in). It includes
  Qt 6 base/declarative private headers, Multimedia, SVG, OpenGL,
  qtkeychain, SQLite and the QML modules; audio and codec libraries include
  PortAudio, PortMidi, ALSA/JACK, FFmpeg, libsndfile, TagLib, Rubber Band,
  SoundTouch, Chromaprint and others listed there. A distribution's
  `apt-get build-dep mixxx` can provide a starting point if source
  repositories are enabled, but can target an older Mixxx/Qt version.
- **Fedora:** `dnf builddep mixxx` provides the distribution's build
  dependencies. Additional current Qt/private-header packages may be needed.
- **Arch/Manjaro:** use the dependencies and build dependencies from the
  distribution's Mixxx PKGBUILD. Also provide a compatible Python 3.10–3.12
  if the distribution's default Python is newer.
- **openSUSE:** `zypper source-install --build-deps-only mixxx` provides
  the distribution's native build dependencies.

Those package-manager commands are reference instructions, not commands
the script executes. Package availability and names depend on the release.
See also the [Mixxx Linux build guide](https://github.com/mixxxdj/mixxx/wiki/Compiling-On-Linux).
Missing dependencies produce a CMake error; the script stops rather than
reporting a successful installation.

## Locations and custom paths

| Item | Default |
| --- | --- |
| Installed Mixxx, install-mode venv/model | `~/.local/opt/mixxx-beat-this` |
| Build-mode venv/model | `~/.local/share/mixxx-beat-this/runtime` |
| Standalone-cloned sources | `~/.local/share/mixxx-beat-this/source` |
| Build directory | `~/.cache/mixxx-beat-this/build` |
| Dedicated settings and library database | `~/.config/mixxx-beat-this` |
| Command, install mode only | `~/.local/bin/mixxx-beat-this` |
| Desktop entry, install mode only | `~/.local/share/applications/org.mixxx.Mixxx.BeatThis.desktop` |

`XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` override their usual
defaults. This profile is separate from `~/.mixxx`: an existing library is
not imported automatically. Both printed build commands and installed
starters select the dedicated profile with `--settings-path`.

```sh
python3 tools/install-linux.py --mode build \
  --source-dir "$HOME/src/mixxx" \
  --build-dir "$HOME/build/mixxx" \
  --runtime-dir "$HOME/.local/share/beat-this-runtime" \
  --python /usr/bin/python3.12 --jobs 2

python3 tools/install-linux.py --mode install \
  --prefix "$HOME/Applications/Mixxx Beat This" \
  --profile "$HOME/.config/mixxx-beat-this" \
  --cmake-arg=-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
```

New build directories use Release and disable tests/benchmarks. Existing
CMake caches retain their build type and test options. Use separate build
directories for different checkouts/toolchains. The script fixes install
destinations to `bin`, `share` and `lib` under the selected prefix.

Close Mixxx using this profile before rerunning the script. Python packages
and verified models are reused, and the native build is incremental. Before
updating, select/pull the desired source revision yourself. Changing
`--ref` does not modify an existing checkout. When moving installations,
rerun with the new paths to create a new venv and refresh the profile/starter.
Remove the old starter symlink before changing prefixes: the script refuses
to replace a starter pointing elsewhere. Python venvs are not relocatable.
Existing profile settings are retained;
before changing them, the script saves `mixxx.cfg.before-beat-this`.

Use `--model-file /path/to/final0.ckpt` to copy an already downloaded official
checkpoint. The script verifies SHA-256 before publishing the file and
reuses matching files on subsequent runs. Failed downloads leave no model
at the final destination. Pip and initial model downloads require network
access; inference remains local. See [BEAT_ANALYSIS.md](BEAT_ANALYSIS.md)
for model provenance and analysis behavior.

To remove the installation, remove its prefix, starter symlink and desktop
entry. Build-mode runtimes, sources and build directories can be removed
separately. Keep the profile if you want to retain its library and settings.
